question: Why must breastfeeding mothers make sure they drink plenty of extra fluids every day?

options.A: To replace fluids lost through breastmilk production
options.B: To flush out the kidneys and stop weight gain
options.C: To help the lochia turn white faster
options.D: To prevent the uterus from contracting too fast

explanation: Breastmilk is mostly water! If mom doesn't drink enough, her milk supply can drop and she can easily become dehydrated.

question: A ward manager is told to cut costs, but management won't let her approve any purchase orders. Which key management rule is being broken?

options.A: Traditional authority supersedes expert authority
options.B: Delegation must transfer ultimate legal accountability
options.C: Power must always exceed formal authority
options.D: Authority and responsibility must be balanced

explanation: Makes total sense, right? You can't give someone a heavy task (responsibility) without giving them the power (authority) to make it happen!

question: Which action is considered the single most effective way to prevent the spread of infections in a healthcare setting?

options.A: Keeping windows closed at night
options.B: Painting isolation walls white
options.C: Frequent and proper hand hygiene
options.D: Changing bed sheets twice a day

explanation: Handwashing with soap and water or using alcohol-based rub removes pathogens from hands before they spread to others. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T5#GNS123_U4_T5_h7)

question: Why might an adolescent with untreated depression turn to substance abuse?

options.A: To cure a bacterial infection
options.B: To improve their school grades permanently
options.C: To self-medicate and escape emotional pain
options.D: To strengthen their immune system

explanation: Teens struggling with mental health issues like depression often use drugs or alcohol as an unhealthy way to cope with overwhelming emotional distress. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T13#GNS312_U3_T13_h3)

question: Which type of evidence is usually the least reliable when checking if a health treatment really works?

options.A: Personal testimonials and individual success stories
options.B: Peer-reviewed scientific journal articles
options.C: Randomized controlled clinical trials
options.D: Systematic reviews of multiple research studies

explanation: You got it! Personal stories and individual testimonials can be very biased, making them much weaker than structured clinical research.

question: Which symptom should immediately alert a nurse to a possible ectopic pregnancy?

options.A: Painful burning when passing urine
options.B: Itching and thick white vaginal discharge
options.C: One-sided lower belly pain and abnormal spotting
options.D: Swelling in the lower legs and ankles

explanation: Pelvic pain on just one side, combined with light bleeding during early pregnancy, is a classic warning sign we always watch out for. Excellent!

question: Which set of clinical signs points directly to neuroleptic malignant syndrome (NMS)?

options.A: High fever, extreme muscle rigidity, and unstable vitals
options.B: Uncontrolled euphoria and excessive talkativeness
options.C: Hyperactive bowel sounds and sudden weight loss
options.D: Slurred speech, itchy skin rash, and low fever

explanation: Think of NMS as a dangerous fire in the body: extremely high fever, muscles stiff as boards (lead-pipe rigidity), and wild swings in blood pressure and heart rate.

question: What makes the enteric nervous system so special compared to other parts of the peripheral nervous system?

options.A: It receives no innervation whatsoever from the sympathetic division.
options.B: It can direct gut functions largely on its own without central nervous system input.
options.C: It controls voluntary swallowing in the upper esophagus.
options.D: It is the only part of the nervous system that uses acetylcholine.

explanation: Even though it chats with the brain, the enteric nervous system has its own local reflex circuits and can run digestion completely on autopilot!

question: What is the main goal of community mobilisation in health care?

options.A: Replacing traditional healers with foreign nurses
options.B: Building more hospitals in urban centres
options.C: Bringing people together to take joint action for health
options.D: Training only doctors to run local clinics

explanation: Community mobilisation is fundamentally about uniting individuals and groups to tackle common health issues together. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T2#GNS124_U4_T2_h1)

question: What should you do immediately if you find an expired drug in the crash cart during a check?

options.A: Report and replace it right away
options.B: Leave it until the end of the week
options.C: Use it on the next stable patient
options.D: Hide it in the bottom drawer

explanation: You got it! Expired drugs can fail when you need them most, so swapping them out instantly keeps our patients safe. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T11#GNS321_U2_T11_h4)

question: What is the main danger of burning medical waste in open drums instead of using proper high-temperature incinerators?

options.A: It releases toxic air pollutants like dioxins into the local atmosphere
options.B: It creates underground tremors that weaken nearby hospital foundations
options.C: It automatically purifies all the plastic materials into harmless ash
options.D: It causes the surrounding groundwater to freeze solid instantly

explanation: Correct! Low-temperature open burning doesn't break down complex chemicals safely; instead, it pumps dangerous pollutants and toxins right into the air we breathe.

question: What is the main job of red blood cells (erythrocytes) in our body?

options.A: Releasing antibodies during an allergic reaction
options.B: Transporting oxygen to body tissues
options.C: Forming initial plugs to stop bleeding
options.D: Fighting off bacterial infections

explanation: Awesome! Red blood cells are packed with hemoglobin, acting like tiny delivery vans that pick up oxygen in the lungs and drop it off all over the body.

question: A patient develops a painful, swollen, pus-filled lump at an injection site a few days after treatment. What is this likely a sign of?

options.A: A mild allergic reaction to clean cotton wool
options.B: An expected systemic reaction to vitamin supplements
options.C: A local bacterial infection and abscess formation
options.D: The normal healing process of deep muscle tissue

explanation: Ouch! When unsterile equipment or poor technique introduces bacteria into the tissue, it causes localized inflammation and can form a nasty abscess.

question: What is a major negative effect of HIV-related stigma in our communities?

options.A: It eliminates the need for VCT clinics.
options.B: It discourages people from getting tested or seeking treatment.
options.C: It increases the effectiveness of antiretroviral drugs.
options.D: It causes the HIV virus to mutate into a weaker strain.

explanation: Fear of being judged makes people hide their status and stay away from clinics. Compassion and education are our best tools to fight this stigma!

question: A woman with a history of Type III FGM comes in for labor. What should the nurse watch out for?

options.A: Total absence of uterine contractions throughout the first stage
options.B: Obstructed labor and severe scarring requiring careful evaluation
options.C: Spontaneous healing of the infibulated scar without intervention
options.D: Rapid and completely painless expulsion of the placenta

explanation: That thick scar tissue blocks the normal stretching of the birth canal, often causing obstructed labor that needs careful handling. Clinical nursing in action!

question: Why might an MRI or ultrasound be ordered for a patient with a rectovaginal fistula?

options.A: To check for active urinary tract infections
options.B: To test the patient's liver enzymes and kidney function
options.C: To evaluate the condition of the sphincter muscles and surrounding deep tissues
options.D: To measure the patient's daily fluid intake and output

explanation: Advanced imaging helps surgeons see the exact path of the fistula and check if the anal sphincter muscles are also injured. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h5)

question: Why is accurate and prompt charting of IV care crucial for nursing practice?

options.A: It is the only way hospital administrators calculate nurse salaries
options.B: It stops patients from asking nurses repetitive questions about fluids
options.C: It provides a clear legal record of care and ensures safe continuity among staff
options.D: It replaces the need for verbal shift handovers between nursing teams

explanation: Good documentation proves professional standards were met and helps the next shift monitor the site safely. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T4#GNS122_U1_T4_h10)

question: What is the main goal of Behavior Change Communication (BCC)?

options.A: Replacing traditional healers with modern doctors
options.B: Ensuring every household buys expensive water filters
options.C: Helping people adopt and sustain healthy lifestyle practices
options.D: Increasing the number of patients admitted to hospital wards

explanation: Exactly! BCC goes beyond just sharing facts; it's about helping people make real, lasting changes that keep them healthy.

question: What is an important way nurses can guide patients and visitors regarding ward waste?

options.A: Revising the hospital's annual financial budget
options.B: Teaching them how to operate surgical autoclaves
options.C: Explaining the correct use of color-coded waste bins
options.D: Training them to administer intravenous injections

explanation: Visitors often toss things into the nearest bin. Taking a second to guide them helps keep our color-coded waste streams pure!

question: What is the very first thing a nurse should check when a patient arrives in the recovery room?

options.A: Maintaining a patent airway and stable vital signs
options.B: Encouraging the patient to walk around the ward
options.C: Serving a full meal to restore energy levels
options.D: Discharging the patient home within one hour

explanation: As soon as a patient comes out of surgery, checking that they are breathing well (patent airway) and that their vitals are stable is always priority number one.

question: Why must nurses look past normal vital signs when checking for gender-based vulnerabilities?

options.A: Hospital accreditation standards prohibit nurses from recording blood pressure
options.B: Social inequalities always normalize automatically without medical intervention
options.C: Physical measurements do not reveal underlying social coercion or lack of self-determination
options.D: Vital signs are completely unreliable when measured on female patients

explanation: A patient's temperature and blood pressure can look totally fine while they are suffering from intense emotional control, isolation, or abuse at home.

question: Which of the following is a primary way the community environment influences health?

options.A: Replacing the need for individual personal hygiene
options.B: Providing access to safe water, markets, and local clinics
options.C: Ensuring every citizen has a high-paying professional job
options.D: Eliminating all infectious diseases from the environment

explanation: Basic community infrastructure like clean water and nearby health clinics directly dictates physical well-being. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T4#GNS112_U2_T4_h5)

question: A new mother who just had a tear repaired with stitches (episiotomy) says she is soaking her private area in very hot water daily for pain. What is the major risk here?

options.A: Instantaneous regeneration of damaged muscle fibers
options.B: Complete prevention of postpartum hemorrhage
options.C: Immediate closure of the surgical wound within minutes
options.D: Tissue maceration and delayed wound healing leading to infection

explanation: Fresh stitches need time to stay clean and dry. Soaking them in hot water makes the skin soggy (macerated), which slows down healing and lets germs in.

question: Which children's condition often needs rectal washouts before surgery?

options.A: Hirschsprung's disease
options.B: Acute appendicitis
options.C: Congenital heart failure
options.D: Infantile jaundice

explanation: In Hirschsprung's disease, a part of the baby's bowel lacks the nerves to push stool out. Washouts are safely used to clear things out before surgery!

question: What is the main goal of vestibular rehabilitation therapy?

options.A: To permanently eliminate all physical movement of the head
options.B: To train the central nervous system to compensate for inner ear deficits
options.C: To surgically replace the delicate structures of the inner ear
options.D: To increase blood pressure and prevent fainting episodes

explanation: Spot on! Vestibular therapy uses smart exercises to help the brain learn how to handle balance signals better, even if the inner ear isn't working at 100%.

question: If a patient has a stroke on the right side of their motor cortex, which side of the body will show physical weakness?

options.A: The right side
options.B: The left side
options.C: Only the lower limbs
options.D: Both sides equally

explanation: Brilliant! Brain pathways cross over in the brainstem, so damage on the right side of the brain shows up as weakness on the left side of the body.

question: Why are pelvic floor (Kegel) exercises suggested for patients recovering from prostate surgery?

options.A: To prevent the development of bacterial infections in the kidneys
options.B: To eliminate the need for any future follow-up clinic visits
options.C: To permanently increase the resting size and blood flow of the prostate
options.D: To strengthen muscles that support urinary control and help reduce incontinence

explanation: Pelvic floor exercises tone up the sphincter muscles, helping patients regain control over their bladder and stop unwanted leakage.

question: Which type of reservoir includes people who carry an infection without showing any signs or symptoms?

options.A: Human reservoirs
options.B: Fomite reservoirs
options.C: Environmental reservoirs
options.D: Animal reservoirs

explanation: Spot on! Asymptomatic human carriers walk around feeling totally fine while unknowingly passing germs along to others.

question: A patient with an advanced illness is physically stable, but their family looks completely exhausted and anxious. What should you do as the nurse?

options.A: Ask the doctor to discharge the patient immediately to relieve stress
options.B: Tell the family to go home and rest until the patient's condition worsens
options.C: Focus only on the patient since their physical vitals are stable
options.D: Include the family's coping capacity as part of your ongoing assessment

explanation: When the family is worn out, it affects the patient too! Checking in on how the family is coping is a vital part of good nursing care.

question: A nurse gives an injection to stop heavy bleeding right after delivery. Which BEmOC signal function is this?

options.A: Execution of assisted vaginal delivery
options.B: Provision of parenteral anticonvulsants
options.C: Administration of parenteral oxytocics
options.D: Manual removal of retained placenta

explanation: Spot on! Uterotonics like oxytocin are injectable drugs used to contract the uterus and stop postpartum bleeding. A key BEmOC skill!

question: What is a primary responsibility of nurses when they suspect a patient is a victim of forced marriage?

options.A: Confronting the spouse aggressively in the waiting room
options.B: Ignoring the situation to maintain patient confidentiality strictly
options.C: Discharging the patient immediately without documentation
options.D: Providing a safe, private space to assess for abuse and offer resources

explanation: Nurses must create a confidential environment to talk with the patient alone, evaluate safety, and connect them with support services. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T14#GNS312_U1_T14_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT a helpful way for a nurse to handle referral barriers?

options.A: Scolding clients who complain about the distance to the referral hospital
options.B: Educating clients clearly on why the referral is necessary for their health
options.C: Linking clients with local transport schemes or community support groups
options.D: Advocating for respectful, client-friendly attitudes among hospital staff

explanation: Never scold a client! Yelling at them only drives them away from care instead of helping them solve their challenges.

question: Why do we use a tiered, step-by-step system for healthcare delivery in Nigeria?

options.A: To make sure every health problem is handled at a teaching hospital
options.B: To restrict patient movement completely between rural and urban areas
options.C: To properly match the severity of health problems with the right facility
options.D: To ensure care is given based on how wealthy a patient is

explanation: Organizing care into tiers keeps things practical! Simple issues get solved right in the neighborhood, while complex cases go to well-equipped specialist centers.

question: Which principle says that a learning task must match your current level of knowledge?

options.A: Principle of Suitability
options.B: Principle of Adequacy
options.C: Principle of Variety
options.D: Principle of Relevance

explanation: Suitability means the task fits your current stage of learning—not too hard, not too easy. It meets you right where you are!

question: What is the main job of endocrine glands in our body?

options.A: Filtering waste products out of liquid blood
options.B: Secreting hormones directly into the bloodstream
options.C: Producing digestive enzymes for the stomach
options.D: Pumping oxygenated blood to body tissues

explanation: Spot on! Endocrine glands don't use ducts. They release their chemical messengers (hormones) straight into nearby blood vessels to reach organs all over the body.

question: How many generations should a basic genetic pedigree chart ideally cover?

options.A: At least three generations
options.B: Five to seven generations
options.C: Only the immediate parents
options.D: Just the patient and their children

explanation: Mapping three generations helps reveal patterns of inheritance that might skip a generation or appear across multiple family members. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T20#GNS222_U4_T20_h2)

question: What does informed consent require before a nurse or doctor performs a reproductive health procedure?

options.A: The hospital management approves the procedure during a board meeting
options.B: The client understands the risks, benefits, and alternatives and agrees voluntarily
options.C: The head of the family gives written permission on behalf of the client
options.D: The local community leader signs a clearance certificate

explanation: Informed consent is an ethical requirement ensuring the patient is fully aware and willing without coercion. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T7#GNS216_U1_T7_h7)

question: How can bad or missing documentation put a patient in danger?

options.A: It automatically increases the patient's hospital bill
options.B: It can lead to missed interventions and errors
options.C: It causes delays in hospital discharge procedures
options.D: It prevents doctors from writing new prescriptions

explanation: Spot on! If care details are missing, the next nurse might repeat a treatment or miss a dangerous change in the patient's condition.

question: Why do some rectally administered drugs avoid the liver's first-pass metabolism?

options.A: The rectal wall completely destroys all liver enzymes
options.B: Lymph nodes absorb the entire dose before it reaches blood vessels
options.C: Lower rectal veins drain directly into systemic circulation
options.D: Medications bypass the bloodstream and enter the kidneys

explanation: Blood from the inferior rectal veins goes straight to the inferior vena cava, bypassing the liver on its first trip around the body. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T18#GNS125_U3_T18_h2)

question: Which of these details do you need to write in your nursing notes after a dressing change?

options.A: Wound size, color, and how much drainage you saw
options.B: The exact financial cost of the gauze packs
options.C: What the patient's family members think about it
options.D: The brand name of soap the patient uses at home

explanation: Documentation must stay clinical and objective so everyone can track whether the wound is actually getting better. You're thinking like a registered nurse!

question: Why must nurses look beyond the individual adolescent patient during clinical assessments?

options.A: Hospital guidelines require at least three relatives to be present at all times.
options.B: Biological markers can only be measured accurately when family is near.
options.C: Teenagers are rarely able to speak for themselves during medical visits.
options.D: Family and community networks heavily shape a teenager's health choices.

explanation: Because a teenager's environment directly impacts their health habits and recovery, understanding their social circle is essential for effective care. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T20#GNS312_U3_T20_h1)

question: A patient scheduled for discharge on home IV antibiotics says they want to stop the medicine early because the pain is gone. How should the nurse respond?

options.A: Suggest waiting until the next scheduled clinic visit in three months
options.B: Tell the patient to double their pill dose to make up for the missed days
options.C: Explain that stopping early can cause the infection to return stronger and harder to treat
options.D: Agree and instruct the patient to take over-the-counter pain pills instead

explanation: Patients must finish their entire course of antibiotics to ensure all bacteria are eradicated, preventing a relapse of chronic osteomyelitis. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T17#GNS222_U1_T17_h9)

question: Which of these is most likely done in a standard general operating theatre?

options.A: Complex spinal fusion
options.B: Cataract lens replacement
options.C: Open heart bypass surgery
options.D: Routine hernia repair

explanation: Great choice! General operating theatres are built for everyday, standard procedures like hernia repairs and appendectomies, leaving the high-tech rooms for specialized surgeries.

question: What is the main purpose of following clinical protocols in nursing practice?

options.A: To ensure patients receive a consistent, high standard of care
options.B: To reduce the salary budget for nursing administrators
options.C: To increase the speed of routine paperwork completion
options.D: To eliminate the need for critical thinking during emergencies

explanation: Protocols provide a reliable roadmap based on best evidence, ensuring safe and consistent treatment across all shifts and staff. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T1#GNS312_U5_T1_h4)

question: Which of these is a very common cause of epilepsy in tropical regions like Nigeria?

options.A: Chronic iron overload
options.B: Cerebral malaria
options.C: Essential hypertension
options.D: Vitamin C deficiency

explanation: Severe infections like cerebral malaria can harm brain tissue. The resulting scars can later spark seizures. Excellent clinical knowledge to carry into your wards! [learn more](GNS222_U4_T12#GNS222_U4_T12_h2)

question: You are getting ready to put a stockinette on a patient's lower leg that has a small healing sore. What is the best first step for that wound?

options.A: Scrub the ulcer vigorously with iodine until it stops bleeding
options.B: Leave the wound completely uncovered so it can breathe under the cast
options.C: Apply antibiotic ointment directly to the stockinette fabric
options.D: Cover the ulcer with a sterile dressing before putting on the stockinette

explanation: Standard stockinettes are clean, but not sterile! Always cover open wounds with a sterile dressing first to keep your patient safe.

question: Why do public health planners rely on epidemiological data?

options.A: To decide where to direct health resources and programs
options.B: To diagnose individual patients in emergency rooms
options.C: To write personal care plans for recovering clients
options.D: To determine the exact cost of hospital equipment

explanation: Population data helps health authorities see where disease rates are highest so they can build facilities and plan interventions accordingly. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T1#GNS321_U1_T1_h1)

question: Which clinical situation typically requires the administration of emergency and critical care drugs?

options.A: Discharge planning for a patient with a healed fracture
options.B: Annual physical checkup in a healthy adult client
options.C: A sudden, life-threatening crisis like cardiac arrest
options.D: Routine outpatient follow-up for chronic mild headache

explanation: Emergency drugs are reserved for critical, unstable situations where rapid intervention is necessary to save a life. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T1#GNS125_U2_T1_h6)

question: What percentage of nephrons in the human kidney are classified as cortical nephrons?

options.A: About 50 percent
options.B: About 99 percent
options.C: About 85 percent
options.D: About 15 percent

explanation: The vast majority of nephrons in a healthy human kidney are cortical nephrons located mostly in the outer cortex. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T5#GNS121_U2_T5_h4)

question: What is the big worry with secondary brain injuries after a sudden head trauma or stroke?

options.A: Cellular damage continues to unfold over hours and days after the initial insult.
options.B: All injured neurons instantly recover full electrical function within minutes.
options.C: Blood pressure drops to zero throughout the entire systemic circulation.
options.D: The immune system completely stops responding to any external pathogens.

explanation: Even after the primary event stops, things like swelling and chemical stress keep destroying tissue over the next few hours or days.

question: An adult patient with a severe disability is grimacing and pulling at their clothes during care. What should the nurse suspect?

options.A: The patient is expressing boredom with the daily routine
options.B: The patient is reacting to normal room temperature changes
options.C: The patient is refusing basic hygiene for personal reasons
options.D: The patient may be experiencing untreated pain or discomfort

explanation: When patients can't easily speak, body language like grimacing or restlessness is our biggest clue that they are hurting. Trust your clinical instincts!

question: Why are progestin-only implants safer for women with a history of blood clots compared to combined oral pills?

options.A: They actively dissolve existing blood clots within the deep veins
options.B: They completely destroy all circulating red blood cells in the body
options.C: They bypass the liver entirely and go straight into the heart muscle
options.D: They do not contain estrogen, which is the main hormone linked to clotting risks

explanation: Estrogen is usually the troublemaker when it comes to blood clots in contraceptives. Since implants are progestin-only, they leave estrogen out of the picture!

question: What is a major worry when pancreatic fluid leaks from the surgical site after a Whipple procedure?

options.A: Pancreatic fistula and infection
options.B: Immediate high blood pressure
options.C: Chronic kidney stone formation
options.D: Sudden permanent liver failure

explanation: Good to know! A leak at the surgical join creates a pancreatic fistula, which can spill harsh digestive juices into the belly and cause a severe infection.

question: How can a severe shortage of nurses lead to unsafe injections?

options.A: It gives nurses extra time to clean equipment
options.B: It automatically gets rid of multi-dose vials
options.C: It causes rushed procedures where safety steps get skipped
options.D: It forces patients to inject themselves

explanation: When you're overworked and tired, it's easy to rush. Staying aware helps us protect our patients even on busy shifts.

question: What is the medical term for when nerve endings turn tissue damage into an electrical signal?

options.A: Perception
options.B: Transmission
options.C: Modulation
options.D: Transduction

explanation: Think of transduction as the translation step—turning a painful physical injury into an electrical message that travels up the nerves.

question: What does the 'drop factor' on an IV tubing package tell you?

options.A: The number of drops delivered in one milliliter of fluid
options.B: The maximum speed the fluid can flow through the line
options.C: The total number of milliliters the tubing can hold
options.D: The hours the administration set can remain sterile

explanation: You've got this. Drop factor tells you the size of the drops the tubing makes, which you need to know when calculating manual drip rates (gtt/min).

question: What is the primary purpose of studying the chain of infection in community nursing?

options.A: To prove which patient brought the germ to the hospital
options.B: To identify the pharmaceutical company that made the vaccine
options.C: To calculate the exact cost of treating a sick community
options.D: To find ways to break the cycle and stop disease spread

explanation: Understanding how germs move allows nurses and health workers to target specific links and stop outbreaks before they grow. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T7#GNS313_U2_T7_h1)

question: What is a reliable way to check how severe a patient's fatigue really is?

options.A: Measuring the electrical conductivity of the skin on the palms
options.B: Using standardized rating scales like the Brief Fatigue Inventory
options.C: Observing the patient's walking speed for exactly one minute
options.D: Counting the number of times the patient yawns during an interview

explanation: Since fatigue is felt inside and can't be seen under a microscope, using structured rating scales gives patients a clear voice to score their exact level of tiredness.

question: Why is assessing family dynamics an important first step for a nurse?

options.A: It determines the exact date the patient contracted the virus
options.B: It helps identify who can serve as the primary care partner
options.C: It proves whether the family has a history of viral infections
options.D: It legally binds the family to pay for all future drugs

explanation: Brilliant! Understanding relationships inside the home helps the nurse find the most supportive relative to assist with care.

question: A nurse is preparing to care for a patient with an airborne infection. What must be done before entering the room to ensure effective PPE use?

options.A: Ask another staff member to hold their breath for them
options.B: Rely on natural room ventilation to clean the air
options.C: Wear any old pair of cloth gloves found in the utility room
options.D: Select the correct respirator mask and check its fit and seal

explanation: Proper PPE selection and fit checking are essential to ensure the equipment actually blocks the airborne hazard. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T8#GNS225_U7_T8_h6)

question: Which cancer is linked to advanced HIV and caused by human herpesvirus 8?

options.A: Multiple myeloma
options.B: Acute myeloid leukemia
options.C: Cervical carcinoma
options.D: Kaposi sarcoma

explanation: You've got it! Kaposi sarcoma causes distinct purple or brown skin lesions and can affect internal organs in advanced HIV. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T2#GNS216_U6_T2_h7)

question: Which event officially marks day one of the menstrual cycle?

options.A: The cessation of progesterone production
options.B: The release of a mature egg
options.C: The thickening of the uterine wall
options.D: The start of menstrual bleeding

explanation: You've got this! Day one of the cycle always starts on the very first day that bleeding begins. Think of it as the official reset button for the cycle.

question: What is one of the most important nursing duties when caring for a patient with a GI disorder?

options.A: Performing independent endoscopy exams
options.B: Tracking exact fluid intake and output
options.C: Diagnosing the primary medical illness
options.D: Prescribing emergency surgical procedures

explanation: You got it! Accurate fluid charts help nurses catch dangerous fluid losses or fluid buildup early when bleeding, vomiting, or diarrhea strike. Essential nursing care!

question: A patient arrives in the emergency ward after drinking kerosene. What is the main danger if a nurse performs gastric lavage?

options.A: Instant calcification of stomach contents
options.B: Chemical pneumonia from aspiration into the lungs
options.C: Complete blockage of the large intestine
options.D: Severe permanent staining of the tooth enamel

explanation: Hydrocarbons have very low viscosity and easily slip into the respiratory tract during lavage, causing severe, life-threatening lung inflammation. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T12#GNS212_U1_T12_h2)

question: Why is fluoroscopy a key component of a barium swallow test?

options.A: It provides real-time moving images of swallowing and peristalsis
options.B: It permanently removes small blockages in the throat
options.C: It measures the exact pH levels inside the stomach
options.D: It checks the patient's blood pressure throughout the scan

explanation: Unlike standard still X-rays, fluoroscopy acts like an X-ray movie, letting the radiologist watch how food and liquid move down the throat in real time. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T13#GNS221_U2_T13_h1)

question: Which test directly confirms a diagnosis of polycythaemia vera?

options.A: Erythrocyte sedimentation rate
options.B: JAK2 gene mutation assay
options.C: Coagulation profile test
options.D: Serum iron and ferritin panel

explanation: Running a JAK2 gene test is the go-to way to confirm primary polycythaemia vera at the cellular level.

question: What are the main hormonal signs that point toward Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS)?

options.A: Complete absence of estrogen production
options.B: Permanent closure of the cervical os
options.C: Hyperactivity of the thyroid gland
options.D: Androgen excess and ovulatory dysfunction

explanation: Spot on! PCOS usually brings higher levels of male hormones along with unpredictable or missing ovulation cycles. You are learning clinical concepts like a pro!

question: Why do babies with sickle cell anaemia usually look completely healthy at birth?

options.A: The bone marrow does not produce red blood cells until the age of one
options.B: Infant blood vessels are too wide for blockages to possibly form
options.C: The mother's immune system filters out all the abnormal blood cells
options.D: High levels of fetal haemoglobin protect the red blood cells temporarily

explanation: Fetal haemoglobin (HbF) is tough and resists sickling. It's only when HbF starts dropping after birth that symptoms begin to show up.

question: What kind of muscle action drives the final expulsion phase of ejaculation?

options.A: Rhythmic skeletal muscle contractions
options.B: Voluntary cardiac muscle pulsations
options.C: Involuntary glandular cell secretion
options.D: Slow, continuous smooth muscle peristalsis

explanation: You're doing great! Quick, automatic squeezes from your pelvic skeletal muscles are what power the final exit.

question: What does the ethical principle of autonomy mean for an older patient?

options.A: The duty of the nurse to do no harm
options.B: The obligation to tell the truth at all times
options.C: The fair distribution of medical resources
options.D: The right to make their own healthcare decisions

explanation: Autonomy refers to a person's independence and right to self-determination regarding their medical care. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T1#GNS321_U3_T1_h6)

question: Which specific questionnaire is widely used to screen mothers for postpartum depression?

options.A: Apgar scoring system
options.B: Bishop cervical score
options.C: Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale
options.D: Glasgow Coma Scale

explanation: Spot on! The Edinburgh scale is a short, trusted questionnaire designed to help nurses catch signs of depression in new mothers early.

question: What was a major legal outcome of the Nancy Cruzan case regarding end-of-life care?

options.A: It established the need for clear evidence of a patient's prior treatment wishes
options.B: It created the very first living will document in history
options.C: It gave physicians the final say in removing feeding tubes
options.D: It banned families from ever stopping life support

explanation: The Supreme Court ruled that states could require clear and convincing evidence of what the patient would have wanted before stopping life support. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T7#GNS221_U4_T7_h2)

question: What life-threatening emergency can happen if a patient stops taking long-term steroids all of a sudden?

options.A: Heart attack
options.B: Malignant hypertension
options.C: Diabetic ketoacidosis
options.D: Addisonian crisis

explanation: You nailed it! Stopping steroids abruptly when the adrenal glands are inactive throws the body into a dangerous crash called an addisonian crisis.

question: A patient with severe nerve pain after shingles is given an anticonvulsant. Why?

options.A: To lower systemic blood pressure and reduce cardiac workload
options.B: To destroy the viral infection causing the localized skin rash
options.C: To calm hyperactive nerve impulses transmitting abnormal pain signals
options.D: To completely replace the need for any physical therapy sessions

explanation: Damaged nerves love to fire random, painful zaps. Anticonvulsants quiet those wild nerve signals right down.

question: What does the FIFO inventory method mean?

options.A: Financial-In, Financial-Out; tracks daily revenue collections
options.B: Fast-In, Fast-Out; speeds up the delivery of emergency medicines
options.C: Fixed-In, Fixed-Out; maintains rigid pricing for all drug types
options.D: First-In, First-Out; ensures older batches are used before they expire

explanation: Think 'First-In, First-Out'! The drugs that arrived first on the shelf should be given out to patients first, so nothing sits around long enough to expire.

question: For a stroke patient with left-sided weakness who is confined to bed, what is the best nursing action to prevent bedsores?

options.A: Keeping the head of the bed completely flat at all times
options.B: Repositioning the patient every two hours and supporting weak limbs
options.C: Restricting oral fluid intake to keep the skin dry
options.D: Massaging the reddened bony prominences vigorously every shift

explanation: You nailed it! Turning the patient regularly relieves pressure on vulnerable skin, while supporting weak limbs protects their joints.

question: Why do nurses perform multiple needle counts at different stages of one operation?

options.A: To follow hospital billing procedures for disposable items
options.B: To allow the surgeon time to review patient notes
options.C: To give the surgical team mandatory rest breaks
options.D: To catch and correct missing items before the wound is closed

explanation: Exactly! Checking at different milestones makes sure we catch any missing item while we can still easily find it. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T8#GNS123_U5_T8_h3)

question: What is the first and most effective step to control external bleeding from a limb wound?

options.A: Applying a loose gauze wrap for comfort
options.B: Massaging the muscles above the injury
options.C: Pouring cold water over the injured area
options.D: Applying direct pressure to the wound

explanation: Direct pressure compresses the torn blood vessels, allowing the body's clotting factors to form a plug and stop the flow. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T4#GNS123_U3_T4_h6)

question: Why do we ask the patient to empty their bladder right before the PET scan machine starts?

options.A: To prevent the patient from feeling claustrophobic inside the tight scanner tube.
options.B: To test renal function and make sure the kidneys are filtering normally.
options.C: To reduce radiation exposure to the pelvic region and improve image clarity.
options.D: To make sure blood pressure remains stable throughout the imaging process.

explanation: You nailed it! The kidneys filter out the leftover radioactive tracer into the urine. Emptying the bladder keeps radiation away from pelvic organs and stops a full bladder from hiding important details on the scan.

question: Why should nurses avoid using cliché sayings like 'time heals all wounds' when comforting a grieving person?

options.A: Clichés are legally forbidden in professional nursing documentation
options.B: Patients find medical terminology much more comforting than simple words
options.C: Using clichés shows that the nurse is in a rush to finish the shift
options.D: Such phrases can minimize the person's pain and cut off open communication

explanation: Spot on! Clichés can sound dismissive and make the person feel like you aren't really listening to their deep hurt.

question: What is a major fear that stops patients from questioning healthcare providers?

options.A: Fear of paying extra taxes for medical equipment
options.B: Fear of being discharged without a diagnosis
options.C: Fear of retaliation or being neglected by staff
options.D: Fear that the medicine will expire too quickly

explanation: Correct! Patients often worry that if they complain or ask too many questions, the staff might treat them poorly or ignore them.

question: Two senior nurses are arguing bitterly over shift schedules, and the manager encourages both to give up a preferred off-day to meet in the middle. Which style is this?

options.A: Avoiding
options.B: Competing
options.C: Compromise
options.D: Collaboration

explanation: Compromise requires each person to concede something, resulting in a shared middle ground where neither gets everything they wanted. [learn more](GST321_U1_T13#GST321_U1_T13_h7)

question: What is the main job of barium sulfate during a lower GI X-ray?

options.A: Lubricate the rectal wall to ease tube insertion
options.B: Act as a contrast medium that blocks X-rays so the bowel shows up clearly
options.C: Stimulate rapid peristalsis and empty the colon
options.D: Absorb excess gas pockets inside the large bowel

explanation: Barium sulfate is a special metallic compound that X-rays cannot easily pass through. This makes the lining of the bowel stand out brightly on the image!

question: What is the primary focus of safe motherhood initiatives?

options.A: Ensuring a healthy pregnancy and safe childbirth for every woman
options.B: Providing free formula feeding to all newborns
options.C: Increasing the birth rate in rural communities
options.D: Eliminating the need for traditional birth attendants

explanation: Safe motherhood focuses directly on the health and survival of women throughout pregnancy, delivery, and the postpartum period. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T44#GNS214_U1_T44_h1)

question: A patient repeatedly visits the emergency ward with vague abdominal pain and bruises, but avoids eye contact and looks at her partner before answering questions. What should the nurse suspect?

options.A: Severe dietary deficiency causing weak blood vessels
options.B: Intentional fabrication of symptoms to get medicine
options.C: A rare genetic disorder causing spontaneous bruising
options.D: Underlying gender-based violence and control

explanation: Recurrent injuries combined with controlling partner behavior are classic warning signs of domestic abuse. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T12#GNS312_U4_T12_h3)

question: What does prevalence measure in a community?

options.A: The total number of existing disease cases
options.B: The number of deaths caused by an illness
options.C: The rate at which a disease spreads rapidly
options.D: The number of new infections starting today

explanation: Prevalence counts all existing cases, both old and new, in a population at a specific time. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T12#GNS313_U1_T12_h1)

question: What action should a nurse always take before having a lying patient stand up to walk?

options.A: Ask the patient to close their eyes and count backward
options.B: Have the patient sit on the edge of the bed with legs dangling
options.C: Give the patient a large glass of ice-cold water to drink
options.D: Massage both of the patient's calves firmly for ten minutes

explanation: Dangling the legs gives the blood vessels time to adjust to the change in posture, preventing sudden dizziness and fainting. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T3#GNS324_U6_T3_h2)

question: A student nurse is getting ready to irrigate an eye. Which action means they need a quick correction?

options.A: Placing a waterproof towel and a kidney basin under the cheek
options.B: Encouraging the patient to blink periodically during the wash
options.C: Resting fingers directly upon the patient's eyeball to hold it open
options.D: Holding the irrigation tubing about one inch away from the eye

explanation: Ouch! Always rest your fingers on the bony cheekbone or forehead, never directly on the eyeball, to prevent accidental pressure injury.

question: A patient notices her resting body temperature goes up slightly during the second half of her cycle. Which hormone causes this shift?

options.A: Progesterone
options.B: FSH
options.C: Estriol
options.D: GnRH

explanation: Progesterone is thermogenic, meaning it naturally bumps up basal body temperature slightly right after ovulation.

question: What is the main goal of delivering an electrical shock during defibrillation?

options.A: To reset chaotic heart muscle activity and let a normal rhythm restart
options.B: To restart a completely flatlined heart during asystole
options.C: To force the heart valves to open and close manually
options.D: To speed up a dangerously slow resting heart rate

explanation: Think of the shock as a quick reset button! It momentarily stops the heart's chaotic electrical signals all at once, giving the natural pacemaker a chance to step back in and start a normal rhythm.

question: What makes droplet nuclei so tricky when it comes to spreading infections?

options.A: Blocking the entry of viruses into the upper respiratory tract
options.B: Causing localized skin infections through direct contact
options.C: Settling immediately on nearby surfaces within one meter
options.D: Carrying airborne infectious pathogens over long distances

explanation: Great job thinking about how germs travel! Droplet nuclei are tiny dried-out particles that stay floating in the air for a long time, letting them travel far on air currents.

question: A patient with a low CD4 count has creamy white patches in their mouth that bleed easily when scraped. What is this likely to be?

options.A: Cytomegalovirus ulcers
options.B: Oral hairy leukoplakia
options.C: Oral candidiasis
options.D: Herpes simplex stomatitis

explanation: Also known as oral thrush, these removable white plaques are very common when the immune system is deeply weakened.

question: Your patient just came back from an upper endoscopy. What must you check FIRST before offering them a sip of water?

options.A: If the skin color is completely normal
options.B: Whether the bowel sounds are hyperactive
options.C: If the patient can walk to the bathroom
options.D: The return of the gag reflex

explanation: Safety first! The throat spray numbs the swallow reflex, so giving water too early could cause them to choke. Always test the gag reflex first.

question: What is a major money-related barrier that often stops women from accessing healthcare?

options.A: Financial dependence due to lack of property and inheritance rights
options.B: Universal health insurance plans that exclude female patients
options.C: Mandatory employment taxes collected only from female workers
options.D: Higher hospital admission fees charged specifically for women

explanation: When cultural or legal rules prevent women from owning land or earning their own money, they have to rely completely on others, making medical bills nearly impossible to pay.

question: Why can a tiny hormone imbalance affect the whole body?

options.A: Metabolic disorders always destroy the nervous system first.
options.B: Hormones travel through the blood to control multiple distant organs.
options.C: Hormones directly replace the need for cellular oxygen.
options.D: Endocrine glands are physically connected to every organ system.

explanation: You got it! Because hormones ride the bloodstream everywhere, an excess or shortage acts like a ripple effect, changing how many different organs function.

question: When handing over patients, what does the SBAR communication tool stand for?

options.A: Staff, Briefing, Assignment, Review
options.B: Safety, Behavior, Action, Response
options.C: Symptoms, Blood pressure, Analysis, Recovery
options.D: Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation

explanation: You nailed it! SBAR keeps our shift handovers clear, quick, and professional so nothing important gets missed.

question: What is a common cultural view in some Nigerian communities that affects family planning?

options.A: Children born in large numbers are automatically given free education
options.B: Large family sizes are seen as a sign of wealth and prestige
options.C: Small families are forbidden by ancestral spirits
options.D: Contraception is required by traditional law for all couples

explanation: In many cultures, having many children is traditionally viewed as a great blessing and a symbol of high status, which can make people hesitant about birth control.

question: What causes the shoulder pain some patients feel after a laparoscopic surgery?

options.A: Strain from lifting heavy objects in the recovery room
options.B: Tight bandages applied around the upper chest area
options.C: An awkward position maintained during prolonged walking
options.D: Residual carbon dioxide gas irritating the diaphragm

explanation: Spot on! Leftover gas can press against the diaphragm muscle, tricking the nerves into feeling like the pain is coming from the shoulder.

question: A patient recovering from an MVA suddenly complains of dizziness, looks pale, and her pulse drops. What is the nurse's best immediate action?

options.A: Elevate the patient's legs and monitor vital signs
options.B: Take her to the operating room for an emergency laparotomy
options.C: Administer a strong dose of oral antibiotics
options.D: Tell her to stand up and walk around to improve circulation

explanation: Elevating the legs helps blood return to the brain during a vasovagal episode, quickly relieving dizziness and fainting symptoms. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h7)

question: What do we call an abnormal, new growth of tissue that forms a tumor?

options.A: Atrophy
options.B: Neoplasm
options.C: Metaplasia
options.D: Hypertrophy

explanation: Great start! A neoplasm is simply an abnormal mass of tissue that grows when cells divide more than they should. Think 'neo' (new) + 'plasma' (formation). You've got this!

question: What was the main problem in drug markets before the WHO introduced essential drug guidelines?

options.A: Patients refused to take any form of modern medical treatment
options.B: There were absolute shortages of chemical factories globally
options.C: Governments completely banned the importation of foreign drugs
options.D: Markets were flooded with too many unverified and expensive drug formulations

explanation: Well done! Back then, the market was chaotic with countless pricey products of doubtful quality, which confused doctors and drained wallets.

question: How should you write entries in a permanent clinic register to keep records safe and professional?

options.A: In shorthand code that only the head nurse understands
options.B: Neatly in ink without unauthorized erasures
options.C: In pencil so mistakes can be easily rubbed out
options.D: Using colored markers to make pages look bright

explanation: Permanent registers need ink to prevent any tampering. If you make a mistake, simply cross it out cleanly rather than erasing it!

question: Your patient has a poor appetite and struggles to finish large meal trays, but they really need extra protein. What is your best nursing action?

options.A: Scold the patient for not finishing their assigned food tray
options.B: Remove all food trays until the patient asks for a big meal
options.C: Switch the patient immediately to a clear liquid diet
options.D: Provide smaller, frequent high-protein snacks throughout the day

explanation: Large plates can overwhelm a weak patient. Giving smaller, nutrient-packed snacks across the day makes eating much less stressful and very achievable.

question: What makes adaptive immunity so special compared to innate immunity?

options.A: It relies entirely on physical barriers like unbroken skin layers
options.B: It responds instantly within the first few minutes of exposure
options.C: It creates specific immunological memory against specific pathogens
options.D: It requires no cellular coordination or chemical signaling

explanation: Spot on! Adaptive immunity never forgets. Once it fights a germ, it remembers it, so if that same germ attacks later, your body fights back much faster and stronger.

question: Which two major legal codes deal with criminal law across Nigeria?

options.A: Constitution and Tax Act
options.B: Civil Code and Labour Code
options.C: Family Law and Sharia Supreme Act
options.D: Criminal Code and Penal Code

explanation: In Nigeria, the Criminal Code is used in the southern states while the Penal Code covers the northern states. Both handle serious legal offenses! [learn more](GNS216_U1_T8#GNS216_U1_T8_h3)

question: What is the main job of a negative feedback loop in the endocrine system?

options.A: To destroy excess neurotransmitters in synapses
options.B: To prevent hormone levels from rising too high
options.C: To amplify initial chemical signals rapidly
options.D: To stimulate continuous runaway glandular growth

explanation: Negative feedback is like a thermostat: when things get high enough, it tells the system to turn down the heat and restore balance.

question: Why do new mothers need close nursing watch right after delivery?

options.A: Because the mother is at high risk for hemorrhage and infection
options.B: Because the newborn baby requires constant intravenous fluids
options.C: Because mothers cannot produce milk during the first week
options.D: Because routine vital signs are no longer necessary after birth

explanation: The body goes through massive changes right after birth, making those early hours prime time for bleeding and infections. Vigilance saves lives! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T003#GNS226_U1_T003_h6)

question: What is the primary focus of primary healthcare centers in Nigeria?

options.A: Basic preventive services and community health
options.B: Complex neurosurgeries and organ transplants
options.C: Long-term rehabilitation for chronic stroke
options.D: Advanced medical research and drug trials

explanation: Primary health centers handle grassroots care, immunizations, and treatment of common minor conditions. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T1#GNS112_U2_T1_h1)

question: How do lipid-soluble (steroid) hormones usually work inside a cell?

options.A: By using second messengers on the outside of the cell membrane
options.B: By blocking enzyme actions directly in the extracellular fluid
options.C: By binding to internal receptors and altering gene expression
options.D: By destroying the cell membrane to release stored energy

explanation: Because they love fats, steroid hormones slide right through the cell membrane, head inside, and talk directly to the cell's DNA to make new proteins.

question: A 38-week pregnant woman comes in complaining of tummy tightening that stops when she walks around. What is this likely to be?

options.A: signs of premature placental abruption
options.B: hypertonic uterine dysfunction
options.C: Braxton Hicks contractions
options.D: active phase labour contractions

explanation: Spot on! When contractions are irregular and go away with rest or walking, we call them Braxton Hicks or false labor. Nothing to worry about!

question: What main effect does digoxin have on the heart?

options.A: It speeds up electrical conduction through all nodes
options.B: It removes excess body water through the kidneys
options.C: It relaxes the coronary arteries to increase blood flow
options.D: It increases contraction force and slows heart rate

explanation: Digoxin is fascinating! It acts like a double agent: it makes each squeeze stronger, but slows down the overall heart rate so the heart can rest and fill properly.

question: A patient has a painful surgical wound oozing foul-smelling yellow fluid. What test should the nurse expect the doctor to order first?

options.A: Arterial blood gas analysis
options.B: Chest X-ray examination
options.C: Complete metabolic panel
options.D: Wound culture and sensitivity

explanation: Correct! A wound culture lets the lab identify the exact troublemaker germ and figure out which antibiotic will wipe it out best.

question: What is the main purpose of community empowerment in public health?

options.A: Forcing citizens to obey strict government health laws
options.B: Generating revenue for local health insurance schemes
options.C: Enabling people to take charge of their own health and environment
options.D: Reducing the workload of doctors in tertiary hospitals

explanation: Spot on! Empowerment is about giving everyday people the tools and confidence to solve their own health problems in a lasting way.

question: What chemical alarm is released by damaged tissues to make blood vessels open up during inflammation?

options.A: Histamine
options.B: Insulin
options.C: Hemoglobin
options.D: Bilirubin

explanation: Well done! When cells get hurt, they release histamine. This chemical sounds the alarm, making blood vessels wider so white blood cells can rush easily to the rescue.

question: What is the most common cause of new-onset epilepsy in older adults?

options.A: Stroke and cerebrovascular disease
options.B: Congenital metabolic disorders
options.C: Bacterial meningitis
options.D: Idiopathic childhood syndromes

explanation: In older adults, blood vessel issues and strokes are the leading cause of late-onset epilepsy because they can leave small scars in the brain tissue.

question: Why is it important for a nurse to ask a fainting patient about visual changes before the event?

options.A: It indicates that permanent blindness is about to occur.
options.B: It helps confirm a vasovagal prodrome rather than sudden cardiac arrest.
options.C: It proves the patient has an underlying eye disease.
options.D: It shows that the patient's blood sugar was extremely high.

explanation: Cardiac syncope usually strikes instantly without warning, whereas vasovagal syncope gives prodromal visual and physical signs. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T16#GNS123_U3_T16_h4)

question: What happens to natural cortisol production when a patient takes high-dose steroids for a long time?

options.A: The hypothalamus rapidly destroys all circulating steroid molecules
options.B: The adrenal glands grow larger to store extra synthetic medication
options.C: The brain stops signaling the adrenals to make natural cortisol
options.D: The pituitary gland increases natural cortisol production to compensate

explanation: Think of it like a thermostat: when there are already plenty of synthetic steroids floating around, the brain thinks, 'We have enough!' and tells the adrenals to take a break from making natural cortisol.

question: What is the main goal of task-shifting policies in Nigerian family planning programs?

options.A: To restrict contraceptive distribution only to senior medical doctors
options.B: To eliminate the need for any documentation during client visits
options.C: To allow lower-level health workers to provide certain contraceptive services
options.D: To transfer all maternal care responsibilities exclusively to private hospitals

explanation: Spot on! Task-shifting helps bridge the gap by training community health workers and nurses to safely provide methods like injectables where doctors are few.

question: Which patient sensation is commonly reported immediately after receiving a fast IV push of adenosine?

options.A: Severe numbness and tingling in both legs and feet
options.B: A brief feeling of the heart pausing or chest pressure
options.C: Sudden uncontrollable shaking in the hands and arms
options.D: An intense craving for cold water and sweet foods

explanation: Adenosine momentarily stops electrical conduction through the heart, which patients often experience as a frightening pause or thump. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T3#GNS223_U1_T3_h7)

question: A patient on long-term traction complains of sudden calf pain, swelling, and warmth in their other leg. What should you suspect?

options.A: Normal muscle fatigue
options.B: Superficial skin abrasion
options.C: Deep vein thrombosis
options.D: Early pin site infection

explanation: Spot on! When patients can't move around much, blood flow slows down, putting them at risk for a blood clot (DVT) in the calf. Always stay alert for this!

question: How is Type II FGM different from Type I?

options.A: It only affects internal reproductive organs like the uterus.
options.B: It involves more extensive tissue removal including the labia minora.
options.C: It is performed exclusively in hospital operating theatres.
options.D: It does not involve any form of scarring or healing complications.

explanation: Spot on! Type II builds on Type I by also removing the labia minora.

question: What is the anatomical term for a joint where two or more bones meet?

options.A: A cartilage bridge
options.B: A ligament anchor
options.C: A bone fusion
options.D: An articulation

explanation: You got this! In anatomy, the official word for where bones meet is an 'articulation'. Think of it as how bones articulate or connect with each other.

question: What crucial equipment must be kept right at the bedside after a thyroid surgery?

options.A: An automated external defibrillator machine
options.B: A mechanical ventilation breathing circuit
options.C: A tracheostomy tray and suction equipment
options.D: A continuous positive airway pressure mask

explanation: Correct! Because neck swelling or bleeding can block the airway fast, having emergency airway tools right at hand is an absolute lifesaver.

question: Why do Registered Nurses rely so much on updates from nursing assistants?

options.A: Assistants spend the most direct time observing daily changes
options.B: RNs are not permitted to enter patient rooms independently
options.C: Assistants are legally required to sign off on drug charts
options.D: Hospital policies mandate daily verbal briefings from staff

explanation: Because nursing assistants spend the most time helping with everyday tasks, they are often the first ones to notice tiny shifts in how a patient is feeling.

question: Why should a nurse remind patients using mydriatic (pupil-dilating) drops to wear sunglasses outside?

options.A: The medication changes the natural color of the iris
options.B: Bright sunlight can make the cornea swell up rapidly
options.C: Ultraviolet rays will destroy the active drug
options.D: Their widened pupils let in way too much glaring light

explanation: When pupils are forced wide open by drops, they can't shrink down to block bright sunlight. Sunglasses save the patient from painful glare!

question: What is a major sign of a 'Theory X' nurse manager?

options.A: Relying on strict rules, surveillance, and micromanagement
options.B: Believing that staff naturally find clinical work fulfilling
options.C: Encouraging nurses to take full autonomy over care plans
options.D: Involving junior nurses in hospital policymaking

explanation: Theory X managers assume staff dislike work and need to be watched constantly. They love strict rules and heavy supervision rather than trusting their nurses.

question: A complete health assessment for an older adult looks at their physical health plus what other key areas?

options.A: Only the financial savings of the patient
options.B: Past employment history from early adulthood
options.C: Cognitive, psychological, and social status
options.D: Genomic sequencing for rare inherited disorders

explanation: Brilliant! A good geriatric assessment looks at the whole person—their mental state, emotions, and family support, not just their physical sickness.

question: A young adult patient has lost a large amount of blood from a trauma, yet their blood pressure remains normal. What is the best explanation for this?

options.A: Young adults are immune to the effects of hypovolemic shock
options.B: The bleeding has completely stopped on its own
options.C: Strong blood vessel constriction is temporarily hiding the blood loss
options.D: The blood loss is minor and requires no further observation

explanation: Strong compensatory mechanisms in younger patients can keep blood pressure normal even after losing a dangerous amount of blood. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T2#GNS112_U7_T2_h3)

question: What is the special thing about a "community of solution"?

options.A: Its members interact exclusively through mobile phone apps
options.B: It forms around a specific problem or shared health goal
options.C: It exists permanently within a single government district
options.D: It is defined strictly by natural rivers and mountains

explanation: Nice one! These groups team up specifically to tackle and solve a particular issue or health challenge together.

question: What makes a well-written nursing goal?

options.A: Focused entirely on hospital routines
options.B: Written only by the attending physician
options.C: Measurable and patient-centered
options.D: Vague and open-ended for flexibility

explanation: You got it! Goals must be clear and measurable so you can easily check if your patient is actually getting better.

question: When is it most appropriate to give a patient an antitussive (cough suppressant)?

options.A: For a dry, hacking cough that prevents sleep
options.B: For treating a bacterial sinus infection
options.C: For clearing thick, green mucus from the lungs
options.D: For lowering a high fever during the flu

explanation: Antitussives are best saved for those exhausting, dry coughs that keep patients awake all night. Let's help them sleep!

question: Why do nurses ask about a patient's job or occupation during a health history?

options.A: To calculate their exact daily caloric intake requirements
options.B: To reveal potential exposure to environmental toxins or stress
options.C: To determine their precise health insurance coverage tier
options.D: To predict their exact date of retirement from work

explanation: Great job! A person's daily work environment can play a huge role in health issues, from chemical exposures to heavy stress.

question: Which hormone does the outer cell layer (trophoblast) release to keep the corpus luteum going in early pregnancy?

options.A: Luteinizing hormone
options.B: Estrogen
options.C: Oxytocin
options.D: Human chorionic gonadotropin

explanation: Spot on! That's hCG—the exact hormone pregnancy test strips look for to confirm wonderful news!

question: Why should you avoid twisting your body while carrying a heavy load?

options.A: It causes the rescue team to lose their sense of direction
options.B: It increases the air pressure inside the transport vehicle
options.C: It automatically makes the patient slide off the stretcher
options.D: It places excessive rotational stress on the lumbar spine disks

explanation: That's correct! Twisting while carrying something heavy is one of the fastest ways nurses hurt their lower backs. Protect your spine!

question: Which of these is NOT a good lifestyle change for managing high blood pressure?

options.A: Engaging in regular aerobic exercise
options.B: Increasing dietary sodium intake
options.C: Stopping tobacco smoking completely
options.D: Limiting heavy alcohol consumption

explanation: More salt (sodium) holds onto water in the body and pushes blood pressure up—definitely something we want patients to cut back on!

question: Why is checking a patient's medications a key part of preventing falls?

options.A: Medications are the only known cause of falls in the elderly
options.B: Pharmacists require routine checks to maintain their licenses
options.C: Older adults always take too many vitamins instead of real food
options.D: Many common drugs cause dizziness, sedation, or balance issues

explanation: Spot on! Blood pressure pills and sleeping meds can make a patient dizzy or lightheaded, leading to accidental falls.

question: What does an autoclave primarily use to sterilize infectious medical waste?

options.A: High-pressure steam
options.B: Dry freezing air
options.C: Strong electric currents
options.D: Ultraviolet radiation

explanation: Autoclaves rely on pressurized steam to reach temperatures high enough to destroy bacteria, viruses, and spores. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T5#GNS122_U5_T5_h4)

question: What role do normal bacterial flora play in the healthy vagina?

options.A: They assist with the physical transport of sperm cells
options.B: They supply blood directly to the uterine lining
options.C: They maintain an acidic environment to protect against pathogens
options.D: They produce hormones to regulate the menstrual cycle

explanation: Good bacteria like Lactobacillus produce acid, which stops harmful bacteria and fungi from multiplying. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T2#GNS121_U5_T2_h2)

question: After a punch biopsy on the arm, a little blood keeps oozing out. What is the best immediate action?

options.A: Flush the open wound with sterile hydrogen peroxide
options.B: Remove the newly placed sutures to inspect the base
options.C: Apply direct firm pressure with sterile gauze
options.D: Immediately apply a full-thickness skin graft

explanation: Simple, direct pressure with sterile gauze is your best friend for stopping minor bleeding before doing anything else.

question: Which nursing action best describes a promotive reproductive health service?

options.A: Suturing a perineal tear following a normal vaginal delivery
options.B: Performing a manual vacuum aspiration for an incomplete miscarriage
options.C: Leading a community health talk on proper menstrual hygiene
options.D: Prescribing antibiotics for a confirmed pelvic inflammatory disease

explanation: Promotive services involve general health education and encouraging positive wellness practices rather than treating active disease. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T7#GNS216_U1_T7_h2)

question: What causes the chemical imbalances known as Tumor Lysis Syndrome?

options.A: Eating too many potassium-rich foods during chemo
options.B: Severe dehydration from vomiting
options.C: Sudden failure of the thyroid gland
options.D: Massive, rapid destruction of cancer cells releasing their contents into the blood

explanation: When chemo works *too* fast, millions of cancer cells burst open at once, spilling their insides (like potassium and uric acid) straight into the bloodstream.

question: What is the main job of a mechanical ventilator when a patient cannot breathe well on their own?

options.A: To deliver oxygen and remove carbon dioxide
options.B: To keep the patient completely sedated
options.C: To permanently replace natural breathing
options.D: To cure the underlying lung disease

explanation: Think of the ventilator as a helpful partner. It steps in to help with gas exchange—bringing in fresh oxygen and blowing off waste carbon dioxide—until the lungs are strong enough to take over.

question: Why is it important to get feedback quickly after a test or practical?

options.A: To guarantee you graduate with first-class honors
options.B: To reduce the amount of work for your clinical tutor
options.C: So you can fix bad habits before they stick
options.D: So you never feel anxious about clinicals again

explanation: Quick feedback stops a wrong practice from turning into a dangerous habit. The sooner you know your error, the faster you can master the right way!

question: Under which waste category do used injection needles and blades fall?

options.A: Radioactive waste
options.B: Pathological waste
options.C: Sharps
options.D: General waste

explanation: Correct! Needles and piercing instruments are always called 'sharps' because of the puncture risk they carry.

question: What is the primary goal of segregating medical waste at the point of generation?

options.A: To break the chain of infection
options.B: To speed up trash collection times
options.C: To make hospital cleaning look neat
options.D: To reduce the cost of buying bags

explanation: Separating contaminated waste immediately stops germs from spreading to staff, patients, and the community. [learn more](GST114_U2_T14#GST114_U2_T14_h1)

question: Which two common bacteria are most often responsible for causing salpingitis?

options.A: Treponema pallidum and Trichomonas vaginalis
options.B: Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus
options.C: Neisseria gonorrhoeae and Chlamydia trachomatis
options.D: Streptococcus pneumoniae and Klebsiella pneumoniae

explanation: Chlamydia and gonorrhea are the sexually transmitted bacteria behind the vast majority of acute salpingitis cases. Great to keep in mind for clinical practice!

question: Which of the following is NOT a standard nursing duty under the Mother-Baby Package?

options.A: Educating mothers on exclusive breastfeeding practices
options.B: Conducting routine antenatal assessments and checkups
options.C: Administering childhood immunizations according to the schedule
options.D: Performing elective major surgeries in primary health clinics

explanation: Correct! Major surgeries belong in a surgical theater with a doctor, not at a basic primary health clinic.

question: How does proper financial control directly help patient care?

options.A: It completely removes the need for doctors to write prescriptions
options.B: It allows nurses to spend less time documenting patient symptoms
options.C: It guarantees that patients never have to wait in the emergency room
options.D: It ensures necessary equipment and medications are available when needed

explanation: When money is managed well, your ward will steadily have the tools, drugs, and supplies required to treat patients safely.

question: If the hospital runs out of single-use syringes, what is the right way for a nurse to handle the situation?

options.A: By asking patients to purchase and bring their own needles from home
options.B: By skipping injections until the patient's condition improves naturally
options.C: By rinsing old syringes with hot water and reusing them for stable patients
options.D: By reporting the shortage and demanding proper supplies before performing injections

explanation: As a patient advocate, you must speak up and never compromise safety by taking shortcuts like equipment reuse. Patient safety comes first!

question: Why do community nurses need to work with other sectors like agriculture and education?

options.A: Hospitals lack the capacity to treat infectious diseases
options.B: Ministries of health cannot function without financial loans
options.C: Health is influenced by many sectors like agriculture and education
options.D: Nurses are required to handle civil engineering tasks

explanation: Think about it—good health depends on food production, clean water, and learning. Teamwork across different fields makes community health possible!

question: A patient arrives with burnt nose hairs, blackish sputum, and a very hoarse voice. What is your immediate priority?

options.A: Apply silver sulfadiazine cream to the face
options.B: Calculate the exact total body surface area percentage
options.C: Administer oral analgesics for pain control
options.D: Prepare for emergency endotracheal intubation

explanation: Those are classic signs of smoke inhalation! The airway can swell shut very quickly, so getting ready to tube the patient is a true lifesaver.

question: Which finding at a pacemaker incision site should you report right away as a sign of infection?

options.A: Mild itching around the healing skin
options.B: Faint bruising fading to a yellow color
options.C: A small firm lump directly under the scar
options.D: Pus drainage and spreading redness

explanation: Pus and spreading redness are classic warning signs of an infection that needs prompt medical attention. Excellent clinical eye!

question: Why do nurses need to ask about the type of creature and time of the incident during an assessment?

options.A: It helps determine the correct treatment and predicts potential complications
options.B: It eliminates the need to monitor vital signs over time
options.C: It prevents the patient from panicking about the injury
options.D: It satisfies hospital billing and administrative record requirements

explanation: Knowing what bit or stung the patient (and when!) helps you anticipate symptoms, choose the right antivenom if needed, and watch for trouble early.

question: What is a common result when a primary breadwinner develops a disabling chronic illness?

options.A: Automatic government provision of permanent housing
options.B: The complete elimination of domestic chores
options.C: Shifts in household roles and financial responsibilities
options.D: Immediate improvement in overall family communication

explanation: A major illness forces other family members to take over tasks previously managed by the sick individual. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T4#GNS112_U2_T4_h4)

question: What common side effects of metronidazole should you warn your patient about so they don't panic?

options.A: Permanent yellowing of the skin and eyes
options.B: Complete loss of the sense of smell
options.C: Metallic taste and dark-colored urine
options.D: Sudden swelling of the hands and feet

explanation: A metal taste in the mouth and darker urine can look scary to a patient, but it's totally normal with metronidazole. Giving a quick heads-up saves them a lot of worry!

question: What is the main functional challenge when a patient has a congenitally shortened fallopian tube?

options.A: The time window for optimal gamete interaction and transport is compressed
options.B: Progesterone production by the tubal mucosa is permanently doubled
options.C: Sperm are completely blocked from entering the peritoneal cavity
options.D: Ovulation is prevented from occurring on the affected side

explanation: A shorter tube means less time and space for the delicate timing needed between sperm meeting the egg and the egg traveling down safely.

question: What is the main purpose of industrial pasteurization?

options.A: To destroy disease-causing microbes in liquids like milk
options.B: To remove all water from canned vegetables
options.C: To freeze liquids solid for long-term storage
options.D: To add artificial colors and flavors to beverages

explanation: Pasteurization uses gentle heat to knock out dangerous germs in everyday drinks like milk without ruining the taste or quality.

question: Which part of the hand is best to use when checking a patient's skin temperature?

options.A: The knuckles
options.B: The palm
options.C: The back of the hand
options.D: The fingertips

explanation: Correct! The skin on the back of our hands is thinner and much more sensitive to feeling temperature changes.

question: What is the main goal of supporting a patient with their medication routine for a chronic illness?
